name: Drupal
support: Open-source software supported by the community and commercial service providers.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, or SQLite. Client: HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Composer modules are used to extend functionality
capabilities: Flexible content types and fields, roles and permissions, multilingual publishing, contributed modules, APIs and structured content for complex sites.
limitations: More complex to build and administer than simpler site builders. Module compatibility, updates, and configuration can require some knowledge to maintain

name: Joomla
support: Open-source CMS maintained and supported by the community and service providers.
technology: Server: PHP. Database: MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL. Client: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with templates and extensions for further customization.
capabilities: Template-based design, extensions, multilingual features, user groups and access control
limitations: Smaller extension and theme ecosystem than WordPress. Major-version upgrades and third-party extensions can require compatibility checks and are more advanced

name: Wix
technology: Managed cloud platform. Browser-based visual editor and CMS collections; front-end components can be connected to structured content. Wix does not publish a complete underlying server/database stack.
capabilities: Visual site builder, CMS collections and dynamic pages, hosting and platform maintenance handled by Wix, built-in SEO and app integrations.
limitations: Less server control, limited portability/migration, custom behavior is limited to platform supported APIs and editor model.

name: Shopify
technology: Hosted SaaS platform. Themes commonly use Liquid templates, HTML, CSS and JavaScript. store data is managed by Shopify. Storefront and Admin APIs support integrations.
capabilities: Product catalog and inventory, checkout and payment integrations, custom themes, apps, order management, storefront customization and other APIs.
limitations: Optimized primarily for commerce. Platform rules and checkout/database access provide limited control over functionality.

name: Ghost
support: Open source publishing platform. users can self-host or purchase managed hosting through subscription services
technology: Server: Node.js. Database: MySQL. Client: HTML, CSS and JavaScript. themes use templates and content is accessible through APIs.
capabilities: Publishing, newsletters, subscription support, themes, integrations and Content API/Admin API.
limitations: Focused on publishing, newsletters and memberships rather than broad modeling, Self-hosting requires server administration, some integrations or advanced features require external services.
